entries.gap: repair_timing -hold makes one pass for each violating end point and then stops, also when violations remain. It also stops at the maximum buffer count (-max_buffer_percent of the instance count; error RSZ-0060). The warning RSZ-0064 ('unable to repair all hold checks within margin') does not tell which of these happened, and it is also given when all checks are met but not the margin.
entries.symptom: A block with many short flop-to-flop paths ends the hold repair with RSZ-0064 and negative hold slack, or with RSZ-0060. The number of buffers in the last row of the progress table is equal to the number of violating end points, or to the buffer limit.
entries.workaround: Read the progress table before you name a cause (openroad adapter, operation parse). At the buffer limit: raise the limit (LibreLane: PL_RESIZER_HOLD_MAX_BUFFER_PCT, at most 100). After one sweep: run the repair again on its own output (librelane adapter, operation replay with state_in of the first replay), or reduce the violating end points before the repair.
entries.evidence: examples/shreg-sg13g2 with IHP SG13G2: 11976 end points, 11976 buffers, worst slack -0.40 ns after one sweep; a second sweep ends with no negative slack (evals flow-repair-progress, flow-step-replay)

entries.gap: The Verilog reader of OpenSTA 2.7.0 and 3.1.0 does not accept the keyword 'signed' in a port or wire declaration of a gate-level netlist. OpenSTA 3.2.0 accepts it. A tool image can have both: the build that a flow uses can be older than the build on the default PATH.
entries.symptom: read_verilog stops with 'Error: 171 <file> line <n>, syntax error' at the line of the declaration. With 'sta -exit <script>' the exit code is 0. The log has no slack line. A script that does not check the log then reports old result files.
entries.workaround: Remove the keyword from the netlist that the timing tool reads (it has no effect on a gate-level netlist), for example with sed after write_verilog. Check that the log of the timing step has slack lines (openroad adapter, operation timing) and that the report files are newer than the netlist. A timing step without slack lines is not run, not passed.
entries.evidence: a signed FIR filter synthesized with Yosys 0.67 and 0.71 (write_verilog -noattr) for IHP SG13G2 (eval flow-no-work): OpenSTA 2.7.0 and 3.1.0 stop at the declaration (3.1.0 with 'sta -exit': exit code 0); OpenSTA 3.2.0 reads the same netlist (adapters/openroad/fixtures/sta_signed_syntax_error.log)

entries.gap: link_design <name> with a name that the netlist does not have gives one error line. With 'sta -exit <script>', or a script that ends with exit, the commands after it run without a design and the exit code is 0.
entries.symptom: The log has 'Error: 1390 <name> is not a verilog module.' and no slack line. A wrapper script prints its last message and ends with exit code 0. Timing reports in the tree are from an earlier run.
entries.workaround: Read the module names of the netlist that the timing tool reads (grep '^module'), and link the name that is there. Synthesis can change the name of a module with parameter values (see the yosys entry yosys-paramod-module-name). Check that the log has slack lines (openroad adapter, operation timing). A timing step without slack lines is not run, not passed.
entries.evidence: examples/acc-sg13g2 used through a wrapper with a parameter value, synthesized with Yosys 0.71 for IHP SG13G2: 'link_design acc' with OpenSTA 3.2.0 gives error 1390 and exit code 0 (adapters/openroad/fixtures/sta_not_a_module.log)

entries.gap: A timing check on a netlist without a placement (no floorplan, no wires) is not a timing result when a net has a very high fanout. repair_design cannot buffer a net without cell locations: it inserts no buffer, or only some. The delay of the cell that drives the net is then outside the library tables.
entries.symptom: The worst slack is more than ten clock periods negative. repair_design reports 0 inserted buffers, or report_check_types lists hundreds or thousands of max slew, max capacitance or max fanout violations after the repair.
entries.workaround: Do not report this slack as a timing result (openroad adapter, operation timing: the status is 'invalid check'). The useful reading of such a run is the logic depth and the stage count of the worst path (measurements worst_path_logic_depth and worst_path_stages): they do not depend on the wire load. For a slack, run the check after the placement and the clock tree, or remove the high fanout nets from the check (a buffer tree from the synthesis, or set_dont_touch_network and ideal nets for a reset or an enable).
entries.evidence: a bank of 24 shift registers of 500 flip-flops with one registered enable, synthesized with Yosys 0.71 for IHP SG13G2, OpenROAD 26Q4 without placement: 0 buffers, 36001 max slew violations, worst slack -158.8 ns at a period of 10 ns, and a worst path of one flip-flop and one cell (adapters/openroad/fixtures/prelayout_no_buffers.log). Control: examples/acc-sg13g2 gives 66 buffers and a slack of -1.1 ns at a period of 7.1 ns

entries.gap: extract_parasitics -lef_res takes the wire resistance from the RESISTANCE values of the technology LEF and ignores the resistance of the rule file. A technology LEF without these values gives 0 ohm for each segment, with no warning.
entries.symptom: The SPEF file has *RES sections with values of 0 or about 1e-17. The exit code is 0.
entries.workaround: Check the SPEF file (openroad adapter, operation spef). See the librelane entry librelane-rcx-layer-resistance-from-lef.
entries.evidence: examples/acc-sg13g2 with IHP SG13G2 and OpenROAD 26Q4 (adapters/openroad/fixtures/acc_lef_res.spef and acc_lef_res_no_resistance.spef)
